name: 5 Gracewell Road, Sarehole
description: This was a hamlet south of Birmingham. The address is now 264 Wake Green Road.
note: Hammond and Scull state that the move away from Sarehole happened 'before the end of September 1900.'

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: 214 Alcester Road, Moseley
description: This house was closer to Tolkien's school and on a tram route.
note: The move away from Mosely happened 'late 1900 or early 1901'

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: 86 Westfield Road, Kings Heath
description: This house was closer to St Dunstan's church.
note: The start date is 'late 1900 or early 1901,' and the end date is 'early 1902' according to Hammond and Scull.

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: 26 Oliver Road, Edgbaston
description: This house was closer to Birmingham Oratory, since Mabel had grown unhappy with St Dunstan's.
note: The start date is 'early 1902.' The end date is when tolkien was sent away to Hove (near Brighton) while his mother was ill.

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: Woodside Cottage, Rednal, Worcestershire
description: This lodging was arranged by Father Francis from the Oratory. It is located near the Oratory, and they are lodging with the local postman and his wife.
note: The end date is 'late 1904,' at least by January 1905.

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: 25 Stirling Road, Edgbaston
description: After their mother's death, Father Francis arranges for Tolkien and his brother to stay with their aunt Beatrice, Mabel's brother's widow.
note: The start date is 'late 1904,' the end date is 'beginning of 1908.'

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: 37 Duchess Road, Edgbaston
description: The boys lodge on the second floor of the home of Louis Faulkner and his wife. In the room beneath is another lodger, Edith Bratt.
note: The start date is 'beginning of 1908.'

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: 4 Highfield Road, Edgbaston
description: Father Francis's growing unease with Tolkien's relationship with Edith causes him to find new lodgings for the Tolkiens with Thomas Macsherry and his wife Julia.
note: The end date is the end of the second week of October.

sources.name: The J.R.R. Tolkien Companion and Guide, Volume 1: Chronology

name: The Voyage of Éarendel the Evening Star
description: Written at while visiting his brother and Aunt Jane at Phoenix Farm, Gedling.

name: Tolkien writes Leaf By Niggle
note: This date is uncertain. Tolkien himself stated in the 1960's that he wrote the poem before WWII began, in the period 1938-9. However, Hammond and Scull reference a postcard from April 1943 stating that he had written the story 'this time last year.'
